headline: Nigerian Naira Falls to Three-Month Low of N1,367.61/USD Despite $500M CBN Intervention
summary: The Nigerian naira depreciated to a three-month low of N1,367.61 against the dollar despite the Central Bank of Nigeria selling $500 million to meet demand.
why: Foreign exchange availability and currency stability are critical for managing import inflation and corporate balance sheets in West Africa's largest economy.

impacts.name: Nigeria
impacts.why: Depreciation increases the foreign currency cost of imported goods and services.

why_moved: Strong market demand for foreign exchange outpaced central bank dollar injections, weakening the exchange rate.
